videos.title: Anthropic Shares Set to Soar
videos.description:
Anthropic shares are set to soar when they start trading on Thursday, after the artificial intelligence lab’s $107.3 billion IPO and private placement broke SpaceX’s record for the biggest-ever offering.

The company behind the Claude chatbot and its seven co-founders raised $81.3 billion in an IPO priced above range, topping SpaceX’s record for the biggest-ever first time share sale, and another $26 billion in a concurrent private placement. The deal values Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

Anthropic’s debut shifts the spotlight in the AI investment boom from companies making the tools to run the most advanced models to the model makers themselves. With hundreds of billions of dollars committed to infrastructure such as chips and data centers, the next test for the top AI labs is to grow revenue fast enough to outpace the industry’s ambitious spending plans.

Angelo Zino, Senior Equity Analyst, Senior Vice President at CFRA, discusses Anthropic's return on investment. He speaks with Bloomberg's Paul Sweeney and Scarlet Fu.

videos.title: Walmart Boosted from E-Commerce, Agentic Shopping
videos.description:
Walmart raised its full-year forecasts for sales and earnings, as the retailer’s focus on prices and a steady expansion of e-commerce continue to win over shoppers across income groups. 

The world’s largest retailer is luring shoppers looking for deals across categories, with share gains in the latest quarter led by upper-income shoppers. Walmart saw its largest market share gain in the food category in three years, Chief Financial Officer John David Rainey said in an interview. The improved outlook suggests Walmart will be able to maintain robust growth even as it laps challenging comparison periods and as rivals recalibrate their strategies. 

Walmart benefited from a boost in its e-commerce business, which grew 23% in the US in the recent quarter. The company is prioritizing faster delivery times, and says it can now deliver to 60% of US households in less than 30 minutes. 

Sarah Henry, Managing Director and Portfolio Manager at Logan Capital Management, discusses the e-commerce strategy, and whether large-scale, global companies like Walmart should be valued as tech stocks. She speaks with Bloomberg's Paul Sweeney and Scarlet Fu.

videos.title: What U.S. Aircraft Carriers Bring to the Iran War | WSJ Equipped
videos.description:
The aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt has arrived in the Middle East to help the U.S. fend off Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, enforce the blockade and give President Trump expanded options to strike Iran should he choose to do so. The warship joins USS George Washington and USS George H.W. Bush, marking the second time this year that the U.S. has had three carriers in the Middle East. 

The U.S. has kept at least two carriers in the region since the war started, and so far five of the Navy’s 11 aircraft carriers have deployed to support the war. Two of those carriers, USS Gerald R. Ford and USS Abraham Lincoln, have set modern-day records for their length of deployment and their time at sea without a port call. The deployment of USS George H.W. Bush, which is in the Arabian Sea, has also been extended.

WSJ journalists visited USS George Washington in the Arabian Sea in October to learn more about how these carriers are conducting operations, and how the war is testing the limits of the Navy’s carrier strike groups. The carrier normally operates in the Western Pacific but was pulled into the Middle East in August to relieve the Lincoln.

videos.title: Nvidia In Crisis: The Rise Of Jensen Huang’s Empire At The Center Of The AI Boom
videos.description:
Nvidia is facing the biggest crisis in its 33 year history, with founder Jensen Huang resigning as CEO Thursday after admitting to having an affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, and accusations of two more affairs with employees inside his company. Now CFO Colette Kress has taken the helm as Nvidia’s interim CEO.

The implications of Jensen Huang’s affair with Alice Huang run far deeper than infidelity because her ties to Nvidia customer Megaspeed put her in the middle of a sprawling effort to accumulate AI chips across Southeast Asia. And Megaspeed is under investigation for possibly diverting restricted Nvidia chips into the hands of Chinese companies.

The relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang dates back to 2023, according to The New York Times. It was a “turbulent” time for Nvidia, Jensen Huang told CNBC during an interview at the time, as the company navigated the first in a series of strict export controls the Biden administration placed on sending its most advanced chips to China.

On that same day we interviewed Jensen Huang in 2023, we also interviewed Huang’s direct report Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, with whom Jensen Huang is accused of having an affair.

Three years later, the long-time Nvidia CEO and founder has resigned, and CNBC takes a look back at our interviews with Jensen Huang and other Nvidia executives to get a clear picture of where Nvidia stands today, and all it stands to lose.

0:00 Introduction
3:10 Before the fall of Jensen Huang
10:02 ChatGPT boom to China bans
13:45 China and other risks

videos.title: HBCUs and the World Bank Group: A Global Partnership
videos.description:
A Shared Mission, A Global Vision for Transforming Lives and Strengthening Economies

What happens when two institutions with a shared commitment to transforming lives and communities come together to advance global development?

Historically Black Colleges and Universities have a distinguished legacy of developing global leaders, advancing scientific discovery, fostering entrepreneurship, and driving economic and social transformation in the United States and around the world. Building on this legacy, collaboration brings together HBCUs' talent, research capabilities, innovation, and global networks with the World Bank Group's development expertise and global reach to create jobs, strengthen economies, and advance shared development priorities.

In this conversation, IFC Vice President Elena Bourganskaia and Xavier University of Louisiana President Dr. C. Reynold Verret explore how the World Bank Group and HBCUs can leverage education, innovation, and entrepreneurship to create jobs, strengthen economies, and expand opportunity, building on a legacy of service and translating shared commitments into lasting development impact.

videos.description:
Anthropic began its journey as an under-the-radar research lab founded in 2021 by seven former OpenAI employees. Now, the company is poised to launch an historic public debut that could set the tone for the AI trade in 2027 and test investors’ appetite for an entirely new asset class. The company that brought the world Claude reported more than $33 billion in revenue for the first nine months of 2026 in its updated IPO prospectus, but also disclosed nearly $900 billion in compute and infrastructure commitments and 90-plus pages of potential risks. CNBC explores Anthropic’s rapid rise, its rivalry with OpenAI and its clash with the Pentagon, and what its public debut could mean for the AI trade.

videos.title: How AI Is Changing Jobs in East Asia and Pacific | Regional Economic Update
videos.description:
How can artificial intelligence (AI) create better jobs, raise productivity, and increase incomes in East Asia and Pacific?

Watch the replay as World Bank economists Omar Arias and Patrick Kirby, co-authors of the October 2026 East Asia & Pacific Economic Update, explore how AI is changing jobs and skills across the region, how businesses can adopt AI, and what countries can do to ensure more workers benefit from a changing labor market.

The discussion explores:
- How businesses can adopt AI in ways that fit local needs
- How AI is changing the skills employers seek
- What policies can expand AI adoption and its economic benefits
Omar Arias and Patrick Kirby answered audience questions during the program, while Alessandro Barattieri, a co-author of the Economic Update, answered questions in the live chat.

videos.title: The Truth About How Data Centers Use Water And Power To Keep Cool
videos.description:
U.S. voters passed 40 ballot measures putting limits on AI data centers this week, as huge 1GW AI data centers from OpenAI, Meta, SpaceXAI, Amazon, Google and more push up water and power bills and put a strain on local resources. One of the issues that continues to come up is water usage, which is needed to cool the GPUs inside data centers running AI workloads. Closed-loop liquid cooling keeps water use low inside many modern AI data centers, but external cooling is still needed to move heat outside of the buildings and that requires large amounts of power or water in hot climates. CNBC visited data centers and spoke to researchers to find out the truth about how data centers use water.
